## Where to find datasets?

- [DATA.GOV.HK](https://data.gov.hk/en/)
- [Census and Statistics Department (HK)](https://www.censtatd.gov.hk/)
- [Kaggle Datasets](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets)
- [Google Dataset Search](https://datasetsearch.research.google.com/)
- [Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org)
- [World Bank Data](https://data.worldbank.org/)
- [United Nations Data Portal](https://data.un.org/)
- [OECD Data](https://data.oecd.org/)
- [Eurostat](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat)
- [U.S. Government Open Data (data.gov)](https://www.data.gov/)
- [Humanitaria](https://data.humdata.org/)
- [IMF Data Portal](https://data.imf.org/)
- [UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)](https://dataunodc.un.org/)
- [Climate Data Online (NOAA)](https://www.ncdc.noaa.gov/cdo-web/)
- [Bureau of Justice Statistics (U.S.)](https://bjs.ojp.gov/)
- [IHME Global Health Data](https://www.healthdata.org/)

::: callout-warning
When looking for datasets for data journalism project, one should avoid **survey** data and **synthetic** data (e.g., on Kaggle, many are created for training ML models), as they have limited value in news reporting. For survey data, prefer authoritative sources like [WHO](https://www.who.int/data) or [Pew Research Center](https://www.pewresearch.org/).
:::
